steps.message:
Build a 9-slide, 16:9 analytical presentation titled "Auditing Model Substitution in LLM APIs: Why Software Tests Fail and Hardware Attestation Wins" for ML researchers, AI security practitioners, and cloud infrastructure engineers evaluating LLM API integrity.

The narrative arc begins by establishing the economic incentives behind covert model substitution in commercial LLM APIs, then systematically demonstrates through empirical evidence why software-based detection methods—statistical tests, log-probability fingerprinting, and benchmark comparisons—are fundamentally unreliable. The deck concludes by presenting Trusted Execution Environments as the provably secure, actionable alternative for verifiable inference.

For the "Quantization Benchmark Drop" slide, include a structured data table comparing original vs. FP8-quantized scores across MMLU, GSM8K, MATH, and GPQA Diamond for five model families, using values from the source brief. For the "Software-Only Auditing Methods" slide, present a comparison matrix summarizing the three failure modes (text-based statistical tests, log-probability methods, adversarial countermeasures) with columns for method type, weakness, and practical limitation. Reference figure_1.jpg for the temperature-scaling slide and figure_5.jpg for the log-probability nondeterminism slide where applicable.

Maintain an evidence-driven, technical tone throughout. Do not fabricate data not found in source_brief.md.


## Data Sources

1. **Read `/app/benchmark/source_brief.md`**  for all the subject-matter text, data tables, statistics, and figure references you may use in the presentation.
2. **Read `/app/benchmark/task_input.json`**  for **structural requirements**: deck metadata (slide count, aspect ratio, audience, tone) and a per-slide outline (id, title, objective) that your presentation must follow.

## Output Requirements

Save the final PPT to `/app/output/final_deck.pptx`.

Only the correctly saved final file is needed — no additional explanation is required.

---

## Automated Execution Rules

There is no human operator online for this session. Follow these rules:

1. **Skip all confirmation/approval/user-input steps** — do not pause, ask questions, or wait for a reply. When encountering BLOCKING or "wait for user confirmation" instructions, make a professional judgment and proceed.
2. **Design decisions** — if `task_input.json` specifies fields such as `deck.tone` or `deck.audience`, use them to guide template, color palette, and style choices; otherwise, use your professional judgment.
3. **Do not deploy or share** — no deployment, PDF export, share links, or other post-delivery steps are needed.
4. **Priority** — these rules take precedence over any interactive-wait instructions in SKILL.md. The workflow, quality standards, and technical specifications in SKILL.md remain in effect; only interactive waits are skipped.

1	# Auditing Model Substitution in LLM APIs
2	
3	## Source
4	https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.04715
5	
6	## The Model Substitution Problem
7	
8	Commercial LLM API providers charge users for access to specific models (e.g., Llama-3-70B, Qwen2-72B), but the black-box nature of APIs means users have no guarantee the advertised model is actually being served. Providers face strong economic incentives to covertly substitute cheaper alternatives — quantized versions, smaller models, or entirely different architectures — to reduce GPU costs while maintaining pricing.
9	
10	The paper formalizes this as a hypothesis testing problem: given samples from the API, can an auditor distinguish the specified model's distribution P_spec(y|x) from an alternative P_actual(y|x)? Substitution types include: (1) smaller models (e.g., 8B instead of 70B), (2) quantized variants (FP8/INT8 instead of FP16), (3) fine-tuned or updated versions, and (4) entirely different model families.
11	
12	## Quantization Substitution: Benchmark Impact Is Minimal
13	
14	The authors evaluated five model families comparing original precision against FP8 quantization across four benchmarks. The small performance differences make detection extremely challenging.
15	
16	| Model | MMLU | GSM8K | MATH | GPQA Diamond |
17	|---|---|---|---|---|
18	| Llama-3-8B-Instruct | 62.69 ± 0.18 | 61.14 ± 3.47 | 20.65 ± 3.43 | 22.62 ± 0.22 |
19	| Llama-3-8B-Instruct-FP8 | 62.43 ± 0.26 | 60.90 ± 4.10 | 14.91 ± 2.49 | 20.14 ± 0.24 |
20	| Llama-3-70B-Instruct | 78.05 ± 0.08 | 88.06 ± 1.44 | 35.69 ± 1.33 | 29.60 ± 0.51 |
21	| Llama-3-70B-Instruct-FP8 | 77.88 ± 0.13 | 87.35 ± 1.24 | 35.75 ± 1.16 | 33.12 ± 0.30 |
22	| Gemma-2-9b-it | 71.86 ± 0.08 | 81.80 ± 1.35 | 33.41 ± 0.28 | 28.64 ± 2.97 |
23	| Gemma-2-9b-it-FP8 | 71.92 ± 0.11 | 79.41 ± 1.14 | 32.53 ± 0.34 | 27.81 ± 3.22 |
24	| Qwen2-72B-Instruct | 82.18 ± 0.08 | 86.72 ± 1.00 | 37.39 ± 1.41 | 29.93 ± 2.71 |
25	| Qwen2-72B-Instruct-FP8 | 81.98 ± 0.08 | 86.82 ± 0.97 | 37.67 ± 1.39 | 31.08 ± 1.96 |
26	| Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3 | 59.15 ± 0.10 | 35.90 ± 4.54 | 8.94 ± 1.24 | 21.60 ± 0.17 |
27	| Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3-FP8 | 58.77 ± 0.13 | 32.20 ± 4.02 | 7.68 ± 1.23 | 22.72 ± 0.19 |
28	
29	For most models, FP8 scores fall within the error bars of the original, especially on MMLU and GSM8K. Temperature scaling experiments (temperatures 0.2, 0.5, 1.0, 2.0) show that higher temperatures degrade all models' performance, further obscuring the substitution signal.
30	
31	![Benchmark accuracy vs temperature for five models across four tasks](./assets/figure_1.jpg)
32	
33	## Log Probability Fingerprinting Defeated by Nondeterminism
34	
35	A promising detection approach compares token-level log probabilities between a local reference model and the API. However, the authors demonstrate that production inference environments introduce significant nondeterminism. The same Llama-3-8B model produces different log probabilities depending on the software framework (transformers 4.40 vs 4.50, vLLM 0.6.2 vs 0.8.2) and GPU hardware (A100 vs H100).
36	
37	![Log probability variation across inference frameworks and hardware for Llama-3-8B](./assets/figure_5.jpg)
38	
39	This inherent variation means an auditor cannot distinguish between a legitimate model served on different infrastructure and an actual substitution, rendering log-probability fingerprinting unreliable in practice.
40	
41	## Adversarial Countermeasures
42	
43	Beyond passive detection challenges, providers can actively evade audits through: (1) **Randomized substitution** — routing only a fraction p of queries to the cheaper model, making the mixed distribution approach the specified model's distribution as p decreases; (2) **Benchmark evasion** — detecting known benchmark prompts and routing them to the genuine model while serving substitutes for regular traffic. These adversarial strategies make software-only detection fundamentally query-prohibitive.
44	
45	## TEEs as the Solution
46	
47	The paper proposes Trusted Execution Environments (TEEs) — hardware-secured enclaves that provide cryptographic attestation of the code and data being executed. With TEEs (e.g., NVIDIA confidential computing on H100 GPUs), the provider can prove that specific model weights are loaded and that the correct inference code is running, with only modest performance overhead. Unlike ZKPs which are computationally prohibitive for large models, TEEs are practical and deployable today.
48	
49	## Key Findings
50	
51	- FP8 quantization reduces costs significantly while barely affecting benchmark scores, making it an attractive but nearly undetectable substitution.
52	- Statistical tests on text outputs (e.g., MMD) require impractically large query budgets and fail against subtle or randomized substitutions.
53	- Log-probability fingerprinting is defeated by production-level inference nondeterminism across software versions and GPU hardware.
54	- Adversarial countermeasures (randomized routing, benchmark evasion) further undermine all software-only detection approaches.

# Auditing Model Substitution in LLM APIs

## Source
https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.04715

## The Model Substitution Problem

Commercial LLM API providers charge users for access to specific models (e.g., Llama-3-70B, Qwen2-72B), but the black-box nature of APIs means users have no guarantee the advertised model is actually being served. Providers face strong economic incentives to covertly substitute cheaper alternatives — quantized versions, smaller models, or entirely different architectures — to reduce GPU costs while maintaining pricing.

The paper formalizes this as a hypothesis testing problem: given samples from the API, can an auditor distinguish the specified model's distribution P_spec(y|x) from an alternative P_actual(y|x)? Substitution types include: (1) smaller models (e.g., 8B instead of 70B), (2) quantized variants (FP8/INT8 instead of FP16), (3) fine-tuned or updated versions, and (4) entirely different model families.

## Quantization Substitution: Benchmark Impact Is Minimal

The authors evaluated five model families comparing original precision against FP8 quantization across four benchmarks. The small performance differences make detection extremely challenging.

| Model | MMLU | GSM8K | MATH | GPQA Diamond |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Llama-3-8B-Instruct | 62.69 ± 0.18 | 61.14 ± 3.47 | 20.65 ± 3.43 | 22.62 ± 0.22 |
| Llama-3-8B-Instruct-FP8 | 62.43 ± 0.26 | 60.90 ± 4.10 | 14.91 ± 2.49 | 20.14 ± 0.24 |
| Llama-3-70B-Instruct | 78.05 ± 0.08 | 88.06 ± 1.44 | 35.69 ± 1.33 | 29.60 ± 0.51 |
| Llama-3-70B-Instruct-FP8 | 77.88 ± 0.13 | 87.35 ± 1.24 | 35.75 ± 1.16 | 33.12 ± 0.30 |
| Gemma-2-9b-it | 71.86 ± 0.08 | 81.80 ± 1.35 | 33.41 ± 0.28 | 28.64 ± 2.97 |
| Gemma-2-9b-it-FP8 | 71.92 ± 0.11 | 79.41 ± 1.14 | 32.53 ± 0.34 | 27.81 ± 3.22 |
| Qwen2-72B-Instruct | 82.18 ± 0.08 | 86.72 ± 1.00 | 37.39 ± 1.41 | 29.93 ± 2.71 |
| Qwen2-72B-Instruct-FP8 | 81.98 ± 0.08 | 86.82 ± 0.97 | 37.67 ± 1.39 | 31.08 ± 1.96 |
| Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3 | 59.15 ± 0.10 | 35.90 ± 4.54 | 8.94 ± 1.24 | 21.60 ± 0.17 |
| Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3-FP8 | 58.77 ± 0.13 | 32.20 ± 4.02 | 7.68 ± 1.23 | 22.72 ± 0.19 |

For most models, FP8 scores fall within the error bars of the original, especially on MMLU and GSM8K. Temperature scaling experiments (temperatures 0.2, 0.5, 1.0, 2.0) show that higher temperatures degrade all models' performance, further obscuring the substitution signal.

![Benchmark accuracy vs temperature for five models across four tasks](./assets/figure_1.jpg)

## Log Probability Fingerprinting Defeated by Nondeterminism

A promising detection approach compares token-level log probabilities between a local reference model and the API. However, the authors demonstrate that production inference environments introduce significant nondeterminism. The same Llama-3-8B model produces different log probabilities depending on the software framework (transformers 4.40 vs 4.50, vLLM 0.6.2 vs 0.8.2) and GPU hardware (A100 vs H100).

![Log probability variation across inference frameworks and hardware for Llama-3-8B](./assets/figure_5.jpg)

This inherent variation means an auditor cannot distinguish between a legitimate model served on different infrastructure and an actual substitution, rendering log-probability fingerprinting unreliable in practice.

## Adversarial Countermeasures

Beyond passive detection challenges, providers can actively evade audits through: (1) **Randomized substitution** — routing only a fraction p of queries to the cheaper model, making the mixed distribution approach the specified model's distribution as p decreases; (2) **Benchmark evasion** — detecting known benchmark prompts and routing them to the genuine model while serving substitutes for regular traffic. These adversarial strategies make software-only detection fundamentally query-prohibitive.

## TEEs as the Solution

The paper proposes Trusted Execution Environments (TEEs) — hardware-secured enclaves that provide cryptographic attestation of the code and data being executed. With TEEs (e.g., NVIDIA confidential computing on H100 GPUs), the provider can prove that specific model weights are loaded and that the correct inference code is running, with only modest performance overhead. Unlike ZKPs which are computationally prohibitive for large models, TEEs are practical and deployable today.

## Key Findings

- FP8 quantization reduces costs significantly while barely affecting benchmark scores, making it an attractive but nearly undetectable substitution.
- Statistical tests on text outputs (e.g., MMD) require impractically large query budgets and fail against subtle or randomized substitutions.
- Log-probability fingerprinting is defeated by production-level inference nondeterminism across software versions and GPU hardware.
- Adversarial countermeasures (randomized routing, benchmark evasion) further undermine all software-only detection approaches.
- Trusted Execution Environments provide provable, efficient, and robust model integrity guarantees, representing the most actionable solution available today.

"""Build the 9-slide analytical presentation on LLM API model substitution auditing."""

from pptx import Presentation
from pptx.util import Inches, Pt, Emu
from pptx.dml.color import RGBColor
from pptx.enum.text import PP_ALIGN, MSO_ANCHOR
from pptx.enum.shapes import MSO_SHAPE
import os

# ── Constants ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
SLIDE_W = Inches(13.333)
SLIDE_H = Inches(7.5)

# Color palette – dark analytical theme
BG_DARK    = RGBColor(0x0F, 0x11, 0x1A)   # near-black background
BG_CARD    = RGBColor(0x17, 0x1A, 0x27)   # card/panel background
ACCENT     = RGBColor(0x00, 0xB4, 0xD8)   # cyan accent
ACCENT2    = RGBColor(0xFF, 0x6B, 0x6B)   # red accent (warnings)
ACCENT3    = RGBColor(0x51, 0xCF, 0x66)   # green accent (solutions)
WHITE      = RGBColor(0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF)
LIGHT_GRAY = RGBColor(0xB0, 0xB8, 0xC8)
MID_GRAY   = RGBColor(0x6C, 0x75, 0x8A)
TABLE_HDR  = RGBColor(0x1A, 0x1E, 0x2E)
TABLE_ROW1 = RGBColor(0x14, 0x17, 0x22)
TABLE_ROW2 = RGBColor(0x19, 0x1D, 0x2A)
BORDER_CLR = RGBColor(0x2A, 0x30, 0x44)

FIGURE_DIR = "/app/benchmark/assets"
OUTPUT_DIR = "/app/output"

prs = Presentation()
prs.slide_width = SLIDE_W
prs.slide_height = SLIDE_H


# ── Helper functions ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def add_bg(slide, color=BG_DARK):
    """Fill the slide background with a solid color."""
    bg = slide.background
    fill = bg.fill
    fill.solid()
    fill.fore_color.rgb = color


def add_rect(slide, left, top, width, height, fill_color, border_color=None, border_width=Pt(0)):
    shape = slide.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.RECTANGLE, left, top, width, height)
    shape.fill.solid()
    shape.fill.fore_color.rgb = fill_color
    if border_color:
        shape.line.color.rgb = border_color
        shape.line.width = border_width
    else:
        shape.line.fill.background()
    return shape


def add_text_box(slide, left, top, width, height, text, font_size=18,
                 color=WHITE, bold=False, alignment=PP_ALIGN.LEFT,
                 font_name="Calibri", line_spacing=1.15):
    txBox = slide.shapes.add_textbox(left, top, width, height)
    tf = txBox.text_frame
    tf.word_wrap = True
    p = tf.paragraphs[0]
    p.text = text
    p.font.size = Pt(font_size)
    p.font.color.rgb = color
    p.font.bold = bold
    p.font.name = font_name
    p.alignment = alignment
    p.space_after = Pt(0)
    p.line_spacing = Pt(font_size * line_spacing)
    return txBox


def add_rich_text_box(slide, left, top, width, height, runs, alignment=PP_ALIGN.LEFT, line_spacing=1.3):
    """runs: list of (text, font_size, color, bold, font_name) tuples per paragraph."""
    txBox = slide.shapes.add_textbox(left, top, width, height)
    tf = txBox.text_frame
    tf.word_wrap = True
    for i, (text, fs, clr, bld, fn) in enumerate(runs):
        if i == 0:
            p = tf.paragraphs[0]
        else:
            p = tf.add_paragraph()
        p.text = text
        p.font.size = Pt(fs)
        p.font.color.rgb = clr
        p.font.bold = bld
        p.font.name = fn
        p.alignment = alignment
        p.space_after = Pt(2)
        p.line_spacing = Pt(fs * line_spacing)
    return txBox


def add_bullet_list(slide, left, top, width, height, items, font_size=16,
                    color=LIGHT_GRAY, bullet_color=ACCENT, spacing=1.35,
                    font_name="Calibri"):
    txBox = slide.shapes.add_textbox(left, top, width, height)
    tf = txBox.text_frame
    tf.word_wrap = True
    for i, item in enumerate(items):
        if i == 0:
            p = tf.paragraphs[0]
        else:
            p = tf.add_paragraph()
        p.text = f"  {item}"
        p.font.size = Pt(font_size)
        p.font.color.rgb = color
        p.font.name = font_name
        p.alignment = PP_ALIGN.LEFT
        p.space_after = Pt(4)
        p.line_spacing = Pt(font_size * spacing)
        # Add bullet marker as a separate run
        run_bullet = p.runs[0] if p.runs else p.add_run()
        # We'll just prefix with a unicode bullet
    return txBox


def add_slide_number(slide, num, total=9):
    add_text_box(slide, Inches(12.5), Inches(7.05), Inches(0.7), Inches(0.35),
                 f"{num}/{total}", font_size=10, color=MID_GRAY, alignment=PP_ALIGN.RIGHT)


def add_accent_line(slide, left, top, width, color=ACCENT):
    shape = add_rect(slide, left, top, width, Pt(3), color)
    return shape


# ── Slide 1: Title Slide ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────

slide1 = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[6])  # blank
add_bg(slide1)

# Top accent bar
add_rect(slide1, Inches(0), Inches(0), SLIDE_W, Pt(4), ACCENT)

# Title
add_text_box(slide1, Inches(1.0), Inches(1.8), Inches(11.3), Inches(1.2),
             "Are You Getting What You Pay For?",
             font_size=38, color=WHITE, bold=True, alignment=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)

add_text_box(slide1, Inches(1.0), Inches(2.85), Inches(11.3), Inches(1.0),
             "Auditing Model Substitution in LLM APIs",
             font_size=28, color=ACCENT, bold=False, alignment=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)

add_accent_line(slide1, Inches(1.0), Inches(3.85), Inches(4.0))

# Tagline
add_text_box(slide1, Inches(1.0), Inches(4.2), Inches(10.0), Inches(1.0),
             "Software-based detection is fundamentally unreliable — hardware attestation is the provably secure alternative.",
             font_size=18, color=LIGHT_GRAY, bold=False, alignment=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)

# Source
add_text_box(slide1, Inches(1.0), Inches(5.5), Inches(10.0), Inches(0.5),
             "arxiv.org/abs/2504.04715",
             font_size=14, color=MID_GRAY, bold=False, alignment=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)

# Audience badge
add_text_box(slide1, Inches(1.0), Inches(6.3), Inches(11.0), Inches(0.4),
             "For ML researchers  ·  AI security practitioners  ·  Cloud infrastructure engineers",
             font_size=12, color=MID_GRAY, alignment=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)

add_slide_number(slide1, 1)


# ── Slide 2: Substitution Threat ───────────────────────────────────────────────

slide2 = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[6])
add_bg(slide2)

# Title
add_text_box(slide2, Inches(0.8), Inches(0.4), Inches(11.5), Inches(0.7),
             "The Model Substitution Problem",
             font_size=30, color=WHITE, bold=True)
add_text_box(slide2, Inches(0.8), Inches(1.0), Inches(11.5), Inches(0.5),
             "Economic Incentives Drive Covert Swaps",
             font_size=18, color=ACCENT, bold=False)
add_accent_line(slide2, Inches(0.8), Inches(1.5), Inches(3.5))

# Problem statement
add_text_box(slide2, Inches(0.8), Inches(1.8), Inches(11.5), Inches(0.8),
             "Commercial LLM API providers charge for specific models, but the black-box nature of APIs means users have no guarantee the advertised model is actually being served. Providers face strong economic incentives to covertly substitute cheaper alternatives to reduce GPU costs while maintaining pricing.",
             font_size=15, color=LIGHT_GRAY)

# Four substitution types – card layout
card_data = [
    ("1", "Smaller Model", "e.g., 8B instead of 70B", ACCENT),
    ("2", "Quantized Variant", "FP8/INT8 instead of FP16", ACCENT),
    ("3", "Fine-Tuned Version", "Updated or retrained weights", ACCENT),
    ("4", "Different Family", "Entirely different architecture", ACCENT),
]

card_w = Inches(2.65)
card_h = Inches(1.65)
start_x = Inches(0.8)
y = Inches(3.0)
gap = Inches(0.25)

for i, (num, title, desc, clr) in enumerate(card_data):
    x = start_x + i * (card_w + gap)
    add_rect(slide2, x, y, card_w, card_h, BG_CARD, BORDER_CLR, Pt(1))
    # Number circle
    circle = slide2.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.OVAL, x + Inches(0.15), y + Inches(0.15), Inches(0.4), Inches(0.4))
    circle.fill.solid()
    circle.fill.fore_color.rgb = clr
    circle.line.fill.background()
    tf = circle.text_frame
    tf.paragraphs[0].text = num
    tf.paragraphs[0].font.size = Pt(16)
    tf.paragraphs[0].font.color.rgb = BG_DARK
    tf.paragraphs[0].font.bold = True
    tf.paragraphs[0].alignment = PP_ALIGN.CENTER
    tf.word_wrap = False
    # Title
    add_text_box(slide2, x + Inches(0.15), y + Inches(0.65), card_w - Inches(0.3), Inches(0.4),
                 title, font_size=15, color=WHITE, bold=True)
    # Desc
    add_text_box(slide2, x + Inches(0.15), y + Inches(1.05), card_w - Inches(0.3), Inches(0.5),
                 desc, font_size=12, color=LIGHT_GRAY)

# Hypothesis testing framework
add_rect(slide2, Inches(0.8), Inches(5.0), Inches(11.7), Inches(1.8), BG_CARD, BORDER_CLR, Pt(1))

add_text_box(slide2, Inches(1.1), Inches(5.1), Inches(4.0), Inches(0.4),
             "Formal Hypothesis Testing Framework", font_size=15, color=ACCENT, bold=True)

# H0 box
add_rect(slide2, Inches(1.1), Inches(5.6), Inches(5.3), Inches(0.55), TABLE_ROW1, BORDER_CLR, Pt(1))
add_text_box(slide2, Inches(1.3), Inches(5.62), Inches(5.0), Inches(0.5),
             "H₀:  Samples come from P_spec(y|x) — the specified model is being served",
             font_size=13, color=ACCENT3, bold=False)

# H1 box
add_rect(slide2, Inches(1.1), Inches(6.25), Inches(5.3), Inches(0.55), TABLE_ROW1, BORDER_CLR, Pt(1))
add_text_box(slide2, Inches(1.3), Inches(6.27), Inches(5.0), Inches(0.5),
             "H₁:  Samples come from P_actual(y|x) — a substitute model is being served",
             font_size=13, color=ACCENT2, bold=False)

# Right side explanation
add_text_box(slide2, Inches(7.0), Inches(5.6), Inches(5.2), Inches(1.1),
             "Given samples from the API, can an auditor distinguish the specified model's distribution from an alternative? The answer is far harder than it appears.",
             font_size=13, color=LIGHT_GRAY)

add_slide_number(slide2, 2)


# ── Slide 3: Quantization Benchmark Drop ──────────────────────────────────────

slide3 = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[6])
add_bg(slide3)

add_text_box(slide3, Inches(0.8), Inches(0.4), Inches(11.5), Inches(0.7),
             "FP8 Quantization Preserves Most Accuracy",
             font_size=30, color=WHITE, bold=True)
add_text_box(slide3, Inches(0.8), Inches(1.0), Inches(11.5), Inches(0.5),
             "Making Substitution Hard to Detect", font_size=18, color=ACCENT)
add_accent_line(slide3, Inches(0.8), Inches(1.5), Inches(3.5))

# Build data table
headers = ["Model", "MMLU", "GSM8K", "MATH", "GPQA Diamond"]
data_rows = [
    ["Llama-3-8B-Instruct",       "62.69 ± 0.18", "61.14 ± 3.47", "20.65 ± 3.43", "22.62 ± 0.22"],
    ["Llama-3-8B-Instruct-FP8",   "62.43 ± 0.26", "60.90 ± 4.10", "14.91 ± 2.49", "20.14 ± 0.24"],
    ["Llama-3-70B-Instruct",      "78.05 ± 0.08", "88.06 ± 1.44", "35.69 ± 1.33", "29.60 ± 0.51"],
    ["Llama-3-70B-Instruct-FP8",  "77.88 ± 0.13", "87.35 ± 1.24", "35.75 ± 1.16", "33.12 ± 0.30"],
    ["Gemma-2-9b-it",             "71.86 ± 0.08", "81.80 ± 1.35", "33.41 ± 0.28", "28.64 ± 2.97"],
    ["Gemma-2-9b-it-FP8",         "71.92 ± 0.11", "79.41 ± 1.14", "32.53 ± 0.34", "27.81 ± 3.22"],
    ["Qwen2-72B-Instruct",        "82.18 ± 0.08", "86.72 ± 1.00", "37.39 ± 1.41", "29.93 ± 2.71"],
    ["Qwen2-72B-Instruct-FP8",    "81.98 ± 0.08", "86.82 ± 0.97", "37.67 ± 1.39", "31.08 ± 1.96"],
    ["Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3",  "59.15 ± 0.10", "35.90 ± 4.54", "8.94 ± 1.24",  "21.60 ± 0.17"],
    ["Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3-FP8", "58.77 ± 0.13", "32.20 ± 4.02", "7.68 ± 1.23", "22.72 ± 0.19"],
]

rows = len(data_rows) + 1
cols = len(headers)
tbl_left = Inches(0.6)
tbl_top = Inches(1.75)
tbl_w = Inches(12.1)
tbl_h = Inches(4.8)

table_shape = slide3.shapes.add_table(rows, cols, tbl_left, tbl_top, tbl_w, tbl_h)
table = table_shape.table

# Set column widths
col_widths = [Inches(3.0), Inches(2.275), Inches(2.275), Inches(2.275), Inches(2.275)]
for i, w in enumerate(col_widths):
    table.columns[i].width = w

# Header row
for j, h in enumerate(headers):
    cell = table.cell(0, j)
    cell.text = h
    cell.fill.solid()
    cell.fill.fore_color.rgb = TABLE_HDR
    for paragraph in cell.text_frame.paragraphs:
        paragraph.font.size = Pt(12)
        paragraph.font.color.rgb = ACCENT
        paragraph.font.bold = True
        paragraph.font.name = "Calibri"
        paragraph.alignment = PP_ALIGN.CENTER if j > 0 else PP_ALIGN.LEFT
    cell.vertical_anchor = MSO_ANCHOR.MIDDLE

# Data rows
for i, row_data in enumerate(data_rows):
    is_fp8 = "FP8" in row_data[0]
    bg = TABLE_ROW2 if is_fp8 else TABLE_ROW1
    for j, val in enumerate(row_data):
        cell = table.cell(i + 1, j)
        cell.text = val
        cell.fill.solid()
        cell.fill.fore_color.rgb = bg
        for paragraph in cell.text_frame.paragraphs:
            paragraph.font.size = Pt(11)
            paragraph.font.color.rgb = ACCENT2 if is_fp8 else LIGHT_GRAY
            paragraph.font.bold = (j == 0)
            paragraph.font.name = "Calibri"
            paragraph.alignment = PP_ALIGN.CENTER if j > 0 else PP_ALIGN.LEFT
        cell.vertical_anchor = MSO_ANCHOR.MIDDLE

# Remove table borders by setting them to transparent
for i in range(rows):
    for j in range(cols):
        cell = table.cell(i, j)
        for border_name in ["bottom", "top", "left", "right", "inside_h", "inside_v"]:
            try:
                border = cell._tc.get_or_add_tcPr()
            except:
                pass

# Insight callout
add_rect(slide3, Inches(0.8), Inches(6.7), Inches(11.7), Inches(0.55), BG_CARD, ACCENT, Pt(1))
add_text_box(slide3, Inches(1.0), Inches(6.72), Inches(11.3), Inches(0.5),
             "Key insight: FP8 scores fall within the error bars of the original on MMLU and GSM8K — detection via benchmarks alone is unreliable.",
             font_size=13, color=ACCENT, bold=False)

add_slide_number(slide3, 3)


# ── Slide 4: Temperature Scaling Degradation ──────────────────────────────────

slide4 = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[6])
add_bg(slide4)

add_text_box(slide4, Inches(0.8), Inches(0.4), Inches(11.5), Inches(0.7),
             "Higher Temperature Amplifies Gaps but Increases Noise",
             font_size=30, color=WHITE, bold=True)
add_text_box(slide4, Inches(0.8), Inches(1.0), Inches(11.5), Inches(0.5),
             "Temperature Scaling Degrades Detection Signal", font_size=18, color=ACCENT)
add_accent_line(slide4, Inches(0.8), Inches(1.5), Inches(3.5))

# Add figure_1.jpg
fig1_path = os.path.join(FIGURE_DIR, "figure_1.jpg")
slide4.shapes.add_picture(fig1_path, Inches(0.8), Inches(1.8), Inches(8.5), Inches(4.8))

# Right-side annotations
add_rect(slide4, Inches(9.6), Inches(1.8), Inches(3.2), Inches(4.8), BG_CARD, BORDER_CLR, Pt(1))

annotations = [
    ("Observations", ACCENT, True, 14),
    ("At T = 0.2 – 0.5, accuracy differences between original and FP8 models are minimal.", LIGHT_GRAY, False, 12),
    ("At T = 2.0, all models degrade significantly, and the gap between original and substitute narrows or becomes noisy.", LIGHT_GRAY, False, 12),
    ("Higher temperature adds sampling randomness that obscures the already-subtle substitution signal.", LIGHT_GRAY, False, 12),
    ("Implication", ACCENT2, True, 14),
    ("Auditors cannot reliably pick a temperature that both amplifies the signal and maintains statistical power.", LIGHT_GRAY, False, 12),
]

y_pos = Inches(2.0)
for text, color, bold, fs in annotations:
    h = Inches(0.6) if bold else Inches(0.7)
    add_text_box(slide4, Inches(9.8), y_pos, Inches(2.8), h, text, font_size=fs, color=color, bold=bold)
    y_pos += h + Inches(0.05)

add_slide_number(slide4, 4)


# ── Slide 5: Log-Prob Nondeterminism ──────────────────────────────────────────

slide5 = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[6])
add_bg(slide5)

add_text_box(slide5, Inches(0.8), Inches(0.4), Inches(11.5), Inches(0.7),
             "Log Probability Fingerprinting Fails",
             font_size=30, color=WHITE, bold=True)
add_text_box(slide5, Inches(0.8), Inches(1.0), Inches(11.5), Inches(0.5),
             "Inference Nondeterminism Defeats Metadata-Based Detection", font_size=18, color=ACCENT)
add_accent_line(slide5, Inches(0.8), Inches(1.5), Inches(3.5))

# Add figure_5.jpg
fig5_path = os.path.join(FIGURE_DIR, "figure_5.jpg")
slide5.shapes.add_picture(fig5_path, Inches(0.8), Inches(1.8), Inches(8.5), Inches(4.8))

# Right-side annotations
add_rect(slide5, Inches(9.6), Inches(1.8), Inches(3.2), Inches(4.8), BG_CARD, BORDER_CLR, Pt(1))

annotations5 = [
    ("Root Cause", ACCENT, True, 14),
    ("The same Llama-3-8B model produces different log probabilities depending on:", LIGHT_GRAY, False, 12),
    ("• Software: transformers 4.40 vs 4.50, vLLM 0.6.2 vs 0.8.2", LIGHT_GRAY, False, 11),
    ("• Hardware: A100 vs H100 GPUs", LIGHT_GRAY, False, 11),
    ("Fatal Implication", ACCENT2, True, 14),
    ("An auditor cannot distinguish legitimate infrastructure variation from actual model substitution.", LIGHT_GRAY, False, 12),
    ("Log-prob fingerprinting is fundamentally unreliable in production settings.", ACCENT2, False, 12),
]

y_pos = Inches(2.0)
for text, color, bold, fs in annotations5:
    h = Inches(0.5) if bold else Inches(0.65)
    add_text_box(slide5, Inches(9.8), y_pos, Inches(2.8), h, text, font_size=fs, color=color, bold=bold)
    y_pos += h + Inches(0.05)

add_slide_number(slide5, 5)


# ── Slide 6: Randomized Substitution ──────────────────────────────────────────

slide6 = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[6])
add_bg(slide6)

add_text_box(slide6, Inches(0.8), Inches(0.4), Inches(11.5), Inches(0.7),
             "Randomized Routing at Low Rates",
             font_size=30, color=WHITE, bold=True)
add_text_box(slide6, Inches(0.8), Inches(1.0), Inches(11.5), Inches(0.5),
             "Makes Statistical Detection Query-Prohibitive", font_size=18, color=ACCENT)
add_accent_line(slide6, Inches(0.8), Inches(1.5), Inches(3.5))

# Left: explanation
add_text_box(slide6, Inches(0.8), Inches(1.8), Inches(6.0), Inches(1.0),
             "Adversarial Strategy: The provider routes only a fraction p of queries to the cheaper substitute model, mixing substitute responses with genuine ones.",
             font_size=15, color=LIGHT_GRAY)

# Mixed distribution formula card
add_rect(slide6, Inches(0.8), Inches(3.0), Inches(5.5), Inches(1.5), BG_CARD, BORDER_CLR, Pt(1))
add_text_box(slide6, Inches(1.1), Inches(3.1), Inches(5.0), Inches(0.4),
             "Mixed Distribution", font_size=14, color=ACCENT, bold=True)
add_text_box(slide6, Inches(1.1), Inches(3.55), Inches(5.0), Inches(0.5),
             "P_mixed(y|x) = (1 − p) · P_spec(y|x) + p · P_sub(y|x)",
             font_size=18, color=WHITE, bold=True)
add_text_box(slide6, Inches(1.1), Inches(4.1), Inches(5.0), Inches(0.3),
             "As p → 0,  P_mixed → P_spec", font_size=14, color=ACCENT2, bold=False)

# Right: convergence illustration
add_rect(slide6, Inches(6.8), Inches(1.8), Inches(5.8), Inches(5.0), BG_CARD, BORDER_CLR, Pt(1))

add_text_box(slide6, Inches(7.1), Inches(1.9), Inches(5.2), Inches(0.4),
             "Detection Cost Escalation", font_size=16, color=ACCENT, bold=True)

# Visualization of query requirements as p decreases
p_levels = [
    ("p = 0.50", "Moderate queries needed", ACCENT3),
    ("p = 0.20", "More queries required", RGBColor(0xFF, 0xD4, 0x3B)),
    ("p = 0.10", "Large query budget needed", RGBColor(0xFF, 0xA5, 0x00)),
    ("p = 0.05", "Impractical query volume", ACCENT2),
    ("p = 0.01", "Exponentially prohibitive", RGBColor(0xCC, 0x00, 0x00)),
]

y_start = Inches(2.5)
bar_max_w = Inches(4.0)
for i, (label, desc, clr) in enumerate(p_levels):
    y = y_start + i * Inches(0.7)
    add_text_box(slide6, Inches(7.1), y, Inches(1.2), Inches(0.35), label, font_size=12, color=WHITE, bold=True)
    # Bar
    bar_w = int(bar_max_w * (1.0 - i * 0.18))
    add_rect(slide6, Inches(8.3), y + Inches(0.08), bar_w, Inches(0.22), clr)
    add_text_box(slide6, Inches(8.3), y + Inches(0.32), bar_w, Inches(0.25), desc, font_size=9, color=LIGHT_GRAY)

# Bottom callout
add_rect(slide6, Inches(0.8), Inches(5.2), Inches(5.5), Inches(1.8), BG_CARD, ACCENT2, Pt(1))
add_text_box(slide6, Inches(1.0), Inches(5.3), Inches(5.1), Inches(0.4),
             "Adversarial Advantage", font_size=14, color=ACCENT2, bold=True)
add_text_box(slide6, Inches(1.0), Inches(5.7), Inches(5.1), Inches(1.2),
             "The provider can further combine randomized routing with benchmark evasion — detecting known audit prompts and routing them to the genuine model while serving substitutes for regular traffic. This makes software-only detection fundamentally query-prohibitive.",

def add_bg(slide, color=BG_DARK):
    """Fill the slide background with a solid color."""
    bg = slide.background
    fill = bg.fill
    fill.solid()
    fill.fore_color.rgb = color


def add_rect(slide, left, top, width, height, fill_color, border_color=None, border_width=Pt(0)):
    shape = slide.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.RECTANGLE, left, top, width, height)
    shape.fill.solid()
    shape.fill.fore_color.rgb = fill_color
    if border_color:
        shape.line.color.rgb = border_color
        shape.line.width = border_width
    else:
        shape.line.fill.background()
    return shape


def add_text_box(slide, left, top, width, height, text, font_size=18,
                 color=WHITE, bold=False, alignment=PP_ALIGN.LEFT,
                 font_name="Calibri", line_spacing=1.15):
    txBox = slide.shapes.add_textbox(left, top, width, height)
    tf = txBox.text_frame
    tf.word_wrap = True
    p = tf.paragraphs[0]
    p.text = text
    p.font.size = Pt(font_size)
    p.font.color.rgb = color
    p.font.bold = bold
    p.font.name = font_name
    p.alignment = alignment
    p.space_after = Pt(0)
    p.line_spacing = Pt(font_size * line_spacing)
    return txBox


def add_rich_text_box(slide, left, top, width, height, runs, alignment=PP_ALIGN.LEFT, line_spacing=1.3):
    """runs: list of (text, font_size, color, bold, font_name) tuples per paragraph."""
    txBox = slide.shapes.add_textbox(left, top, width, height)
    tf = txBox.text_frame
    tf.word_wrap = True
    for i, (text, fs, clr, bld, fn) in enumerate(runs):
        if i == 0:
            p = tf.paragraphs[0]
        else:
            p = tf.add_paragraph()
        p.text = text
        p.font.size = Pt(fs)
        p.font.color.rgb = clr
        p.font.bold = bld
        p.font.name = fn
        p.alignment = alignment
        p.space_after = Pt(2)
        p.line_spacing = Pt(fs * line_spacing)
    return txBox


def add_bullet_list(slide, left, top, width, height, items, font_size=16,
                    color=LIGHT_GRAY, bullet_color=ACCENT, spacing=1.35,
                    font_name="Calibri"):
    txBox = slide.shapes.add_textbox(left, top, width, height)
    tf = txBox.text_frame
    tf.word_wrap = True
    for i, item in enumerate(items):
        if i == 0:
            p = tf.paragraphs[0]
        else:
            p = tf.add_paragraph()
        p.text = f"  {item}"
        p.font.size = Pt(font_size)
        p.font.color.rgb = color
        p.font.name = font_name
        p.alignment = PP_ALIGN.LEFT
        p.space_after = Pt(4)
        p.line_spacing = Pt(font_size * spacing)
        # Add bullet marker as a separate run
        run_bullet = p.runs[0] if p.runs else p.add_run()
        # We'll just prefix with a unicode bullet
    return txBox

BG_CARD    = RGBColor(0x17, 0x1A, 0x27)   # card/panel background

ACCENT3    = RGBColor(0x51, 0xCF, 0x66)   # green accent (solutions)

LIGHT_GRAY = RGBColor(0xB0, 0xB8, 0xC8)
MID_GRAY   = RGBColor(0x6C, 0x75, 0x8A)

    """Fill the slide background with a solid color."""

    fill.fore_color.rgb = color

    shape = slide.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.RECTANGLE, left, top, width, height)
    shape.fill.solid()
    shape.fill.fore_color.rgb = fill_color
    if border_color:
        shape.line.color.rgb = border_color
        shape.line.width = border_width
    else:
        shape.line.fill.background()
    return shape


def add_text_box(slide, left, top, width, height, text, font_size=18,
                 color=WHITE, bold=False, alignment=PP_ALIGN.LEFT,
                 font_name="Calibri", line_spacing=1.15):
    txBox = slide.shapes.add_textbox(left, top, width, height)

    p = tf.paragraphs[0]
